current.text: Toronto traded for Kawhi Leonard and lost Brandon Ingram. Barrett is a projected starter next to Quickley, Leonard, Barnes and Poeltl.
He is expected to lose usage to Kawhi Leonard. One expert calls him the biggest loser of the trade.
He should start and play 30 or more minutes. Kawhi Leonard's load management helps him, and he should step up when Kawhi is out.
By the numbers, he was Toronto's most impactful offensive player last season.
One expert expects him to finish at an impressive level next to Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes.
His contract situation could make him a trade candidate by the deadline if Toronto starts the season badly.
In category leagues, experts rank him outside the top 130 and say a pick around 107 is too early. Around pick 120, one expert is fine with drafting him.
Toronto is projected to win about 52 games. The team is not deep after its top seven.
Toronto has 15 back-to-backs, with three of them in the playoffs.

durable.text: He is mainly a scorer. His steals and blocks are low and his efficiency is modest.
He is worth much more in points leagues than in category leagues.
His FT% is low for his volume of free throws, which clearly hurts a team's FT%.

note: Barrett is a 1 USD player on both Yahoo and ESPN. He also went for 1 USD in our league last season, and his ranks of 132 to 139 put him near the edge of the 144 players drafted. His value is points (18.5 projected) with a few threes and rebounds. His 68.7% FT and weak steals and blocks limit him, so he fits best as a cheap last-dollar scorer on a team punting FT%. Early in the season, check how much usage he keeps next to Kawhi Leonard and whether his minutes rise when Kawhi rests.
